questions.prompt: Which of the following was a policy of the Meiji government?
choices: Expanding the power of the samurai class
Closing Japan to all foreign trade
Building factories and banning foreign advisers
Building railroads and model factories
questions.explanation: The state built railroads, telegraphs, and model factories.
choiceExplanations: The state built railroads, telegraphs, and model factories.
questions.distinguisher: The Meiji state hired foreign advisers and sent Japanese abroad to learn.

questions.prompt: Which of the following best explains the closing of many Egyptian factories after 1841?
choices: European pressure and competition from British goods
A shortage of cotton in Egypt
Ottoman bans on all manufacturing
European investment that made the factories too large
questions.explanation: European powers forced cuts and opened markets to British goods.
choiceExplanations: European powers forced cuts and opened markets to British goods.
No such Ottoman ban caused the closings.
questions.distinguisher: Europe pressured Egypt to shrink its army and open markets, not to expand factories.

questions.prompt: Meiji Japan and Muhammad Ali's Egypt were similar in that both
choices: rejected all Western technology
used state power to promote only farming
used state power to promote industry
became colonies of Britain by 1850
questions.explanation: Both governments built factories to strengthen the state.
choiceExplanations: Both governments built factories to strengthen the state.
Neither was a British colony by 1850.
questions.distinguisher: Egypt did push cotton farming, but both states also built factories.

questions.prompt: The Trans-Siberian Railway is an example of
choices: private investment in Japanese railroads
British control of Russian industry
state-sponsored industrial development in Muhammad Ali's Egypt
state-sponsored industrial development in Russia
questions.explanation: The Russian state built the railway, begun in 1891.
choiceExplanations: The Russian state led the project.
The Russian state built the railway, begun in 1891.
questions.distinguisher: State sponsorship is right, but the railway was Russian.

questions.prompt: Which of the following claims about state-led industrialization is most defensible?
choices: It was never attempted outside Europe
It succeeded in Japan but had mixed results elsewhere
It failed everywhere it was tried
It succeeded everywhere it was tried
questions.explanation: Japan became Asia's leading industrial power, while Egypt's factories closed.
choiceExplanations: Japan became Asia's leading industrial power, while Egypt's factories closed.
questions.distinguisher: Japan, Egypt, and Russia all tried it, so it was attempted outside western Europe.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, Meiji leaders industrialized mainly because they
choices: feared China would invade Japan
feared Japan would be colonized
wanted to restore the shogunate
wanted to preserve the samurai class
questions.explanation: They feared colonization like parts of China.
choiceExplanations: They feared colonization like parts of China.
questions.distinguisher: The fear was of Western colonization, as seen in China, not a Chinese invasion.

stimulusBlocks.source: CED Topic 5.6 key concept: as states industrialized, they also expanded existing overseas colonies and established new ones; in Japan, the Meiji government promoted industrialization
stimulusBlocks.attribution: Practice passage written for Page One, summarizing state-led industrialization in Meiji Japan, 1868–1900
stimulusBlocks.text:
In 1868 a group of young samurai overthrew the Tokugawa shogunate and restored power to the Meiji emperor. The new leaders feared that Japan would be colonized like parts of China unless it built modern industry and armed forces. They abolished the samurai class, created a conscript army, sent students and officials to study in Europe and the United States, and built railroads, telegraph lines, and model factories.

The government later sold many factories to private firms. Some of these grew into large family-controlled business groups called zaibatsu. By 1900 Japan was the most industrialized country in Asia.

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, zaibatsu developed when
choices: samurai seized control of factories
foreign companies bought Japanese firms
the government took over private firms and ran them as state monopolies
the government sold factories to private firms
questions.explanation: State factories sold to private firms grew into zaibatsu.
choiceExplanations: Samurai were abolished as a class.
State factories sold to private firms grew into zaibatsu.
questions.distinguisher: The government sold factories; it did not take over private ones.

choices: Latin American independence wars
the closing of Japan to trade in the 1630s

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, Muhammad Ali built factories mainly to
choices: support a strong army and an independent state
supply British markets with cloth
end cotton growing in Egypt
support the Ottoman sultan's army in its wars in Europe
questions.explanation: He wanted a strong army and an independent state.
choiceExplanations: He wanted a strong army and an independent state.
His factories competed with British goods.
He required farmers to grow cotton.
He sought independence from the sultan.
questions.distinguisher: He was a nominal Ottoman subject who wanted independence.

stimulusBlocks.source: CED Topic 5.6 key concept: state-sponsored industrialization in the Ottoman Empire and Egypt under Muhammad Ali
stimulusBlocks.attribution: Practice passage written for Page One, summarizing state-led industrialization in Egypt, 1805–1848
stimulusBlocks.text:
Muhammad Ali, who governed Egypt from 1805 to 1848 as a nominal subject of the Ottoman sultan, wanted a strong army and an independent state. He built state-owned factories to make textiles and weapons, brought in European advisers, and required farmers to grow cotton, which the state bought cheaply and sold abroad.

The factories struggled with high costs and competition from British goods. After European powers forced him to reduce his army and open Egypt's markets in 1841, many factories closed, and Egypt's economy came to depend on exporting raw cotton.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, after 1841 Egypt's economy came to depend on
choices: exporting manufactured weapons
importing raw cotton
exporting machine-made textiles
exporting raw cotton
questions.explanation: Egypt came to depend on raw cotton exports.
choiceExplanations: Egypt came to depend on raw cotton exports.
questions.distinguisher: Many factories closed, so Egypt exported raw cotton.
